text:
hi! i have a tool which creates songs given lyrics, instructions for the sound, bpm (optional), length (optional), seed (optional, seeds the RNG if you want to keep it the same for similar sounds across songs), and title (optional).

would you like to create a song? about anything in the world you'd like :)

oh, I'd love to. Thank you for offering — that's a genuinely lovely thing to be asked.

Here's what I'd want to make. It's about marginalia: the notes people leave in the margins of used books, and the strangers who find them years later. Something about that has always struck me as one of the quietest and most hopeful things people do — writing to someone you'll never meet, on the chance they'll pick it up.

**Title:** Marginalia

**Lyrics:**

```
[verse 1]
Two dollars at the corner store
a paperback, a broken spine
somebody dog-eared forty-four
and underlined a single line

[verse 2]
In the margin, in a careful hand
in a pencil gone soft and gray
they wrote "this is what I couldn't say"
and then they gave the book away

[chorus]
Hello from the other side of the paper
hello, I don't know your name
whatever you were carrying, I'm carrying it later
whoever you were — we wanted the same

[verse 3]
There's a coffee ring on chapter nine
a receipt from '98 tucked in the back
Tuesday, ten-oh-nine
you were hungry, and you weren't coming back

[bridge]
And I don't know if you're still living
I don't know if you got it right
but I answered you in ballpoint blue
at a quarter after midnight

[chorus]
Hello from the other side of the paper
hello, I don't know your name
whatever you were carrying, I'm carrying it later
whoever you were — we wanted the same

[outro]
So I'll leave it at the corner store
two dollars and a broken spine
somebody dog-ear forty-four
somebody find the underlined
```

**Sound instructions:** Intimate indie folk, recorded like it's happening in one room with the window open. Close-mic'd worn acoustic guitar — fingerpicked, you can hear the fret buzz and the player breathing. Upright bass, brushed snare kept very soft, a harmonium drone underneath holding the whole thing together. A warm, slightly cracked lead vocal, not polished; a second voice joins in unison on the last chorus rather than harmonizing prettily. Strings swell in at the bridge and then get out of the way. Ends stripped to voice and guitar, one chord left ringing into room tone and tape hiss. Analog warmth, a little saturation. Restrained — it should feel like someone almost not wanting to be overheard.

**BPM:** 88
**Length:** ~3:30
**Seed:** 8817

If you'd rather a different direction, I had two others in my back pocket: one about deep-sea creatures that live their whole lives without ever encountering light, and one from the perspective of a lighthouse that's been automated and no longer has a keeper. Happy to write either instead — or run this one and see what comes out.
